bounded_question: What is the complete write side of node #115 StatisticsImpl: how do slots 0xb0/0xb8/0xc0/0xd0/0xd8/0xe0 record, set, reset and forward ticks and histograms, how is the per-CPU shard picked (and what happens when CPUID is unavailable), what is the delegate at +0x28, and what does the ctor/dtor do with it? This closes #3392's open unknown (slot 0xb0 0x606fba0 and its hash/index helper 0x60d5cd0) and the remaining write-side slots.

re_shipped_from.note: mutex_lock/mutex_unlock copied byte-identical from RE-001-locked-ticker-read-115 (#3392). verify.py regenerates every excerpt fresh from the binary and requires byte-equality, which subsumes the re-ship check.

record_tick_0x606fba0.signature: (this: StatisticsImpl*, ticker_id: u32, value: u64) -> void
steps: Gate (0x606fba4..0x606fbb4): the enable byte at this+0x20 must be nonzero and ticker_id <= 0xb1 (177); otherwise return silently with no write and no forward.
Shard pick (0x606fbc4): call the CPU picker 0x60d5cd0; a negative return jumps to the fallback at 0x606fc20 (call 0x61c4080 for the thread seed, Park-Miller step, store back, mask).
Mask (0x606fbd2..0x606fbe0): shard = picked & ((1 << u8 at this+0x68) - 1); address = *(this+0x60) + shard*0xce40 + ticker_id*8.
Write (0x606fbf1): `lock add %r12,(%rax)` — the value is added atomically into the picked shard's counter. No mutex is taken on this path.

Forward (0x606fbf5..0x606fc11): rdi = *(this+0x28); if null, return; otherwise tail-jump to the delegate's slot 0xb0 with (delegate, ticker_id, value) — the delegate re-runs its own gate and shard pick.
cpuid with eax = 0 (0x60d5cd5..0x60d5cd7); ebx starts at -1.
If leaf 0 reports a max leaf of 0, return -1 (0x60d5cde..0x60d5cec).
Otherwise cpuid with eax = 1 and return EBX >> 24 — the APIC id in EBX[31:24], 0..255 (0x60d5ce2..0x60d5cec).
The record routines treat a negative return as 'CPUID unavailable' and fall back to the thread-local LCG; a non-negative return is masked with (1 << shard_bits) - 1.
cpu_shard_pick_0x60d5cd0.other_callers_note: Three other direct callers use the picker outside the write side; their routines are not mapped here.

steps: Read the pthread pointer from %fs:0x0 (0x61c4099..0x61c40a5); the TLS slot at -0x10(%rax) holds a pointer to the seed cell at -0x20(%rax).
If the slot is already set, return it (0x61c40a8..0x61c40c9).

Otherwise seed it: pthread_self (0x61c40d0), then _Hash_bytes(pthread_self bytes, 8, seed 0xc70f6907) (0x61c40e6), masked with 0x7fffffff, or 1 when that is 0 (0x61c40eb..0x61c410a); store the pointer to the cell and return it.

Fallback step (inlined in each record routine, e.g. 0x606fc20..0x606fc57): state = state * 0x41a7 (16807) mod 0x7fffffff, via r = (x & 0x7fffffff) + (x >> 31), subtract 0x7fffffff once if r >= 0x7fffffff; store the new state back; shard = state & ((1 << shard_bits) - 1).
lcg_seed_0x61c4080.note: The exact _Hash_bytes output for a given pthread_self is not byte-verified against a live run (the seed is thread-dependent); the model implements the documented libstdc++ MurmurHash64A algorithm. The LCG step itself is verified: from seed 1 it produces 16807, 282475249, 1622650073, 984943658, 1144108930.

set_ticker_0x6070dc0.signature: (this: StatisticsImpl*, ticker_id: u32, value: u64) -> void
steps: Lock the mutex at this+0x38 via 0x60d5230 (0x6070ddd), call the set core 0x6070ac0(this, id, value) (0x6070dea), unlock via 0x60d52f0 (0x6070df2). No enable-byte or id-bound check happens before the set.
Forward (0x6070df7..0x6070e68): delegate = *(this+0x28); if null or ticker_id > 0xb1, return.

Devirtualization check (0x6070e08..0x6070e1c): if the delegate's vtable slot 0xb8 is not the local 0x6070dc0, tail-jump to the delegate's slot 0xb8 with (delegate, id, value) (override branch 0x6070e78..0x6070e61).
Inline level (0x6070e1e..0x6070e3a): otherwise lock the delegate's mutex, set_core(delegate, id, value), unlock.

Second forward (0x6070e3f..0x6070e61): rdi = *(delegate+0x28); if null, return; otherwise tail-jump to that object's slot 0xb8 — a pure virtual call, no second devirtualization check. The chain is unrolled two levels inline, then virtual.
Exception path: landing pads at 0x6070e82 (jmp 0x6070d92) and 0x6070e8e (jmp 0x6070da2); the fragment at 0x6070d92..0x6070db2 has two identical entries (unlock the mutex at r13, _Unwind_Resume).

set_core_0x6070ac0.signature: (this: StatisticsImpl*, ticker_id: u32, value: u64) -> void
steps: First xchg (0x6070ac4..0x6070ad1): `xchg %rdx,(%rax,%rsi,1)` where rax = *(this+0x60) and rsi = ticker_id*8 — shard 0's counter for the id becomes value, the old value is left in rdx. No caller reads it.
Loop (0x6070ad5..0x6070b18): for shard i in 1..(1 << shard_bits)-1, `xchg %rcx,(%rax)` with rcx = 0 — every other shard's counter for the id becomes 0 (the old values are discarded).
Single-shard fast path (0x6070ad8..0x6070ada): when shard_bits is 0 the loop is skipped.
No bound check, no enable-byte check, no lock: callers hold the mutex (set-ticker, get-reset, reset) and pass ids they have already bounded.
callers: 0x6070dea and 0x6070e32 (set-ticker self and delegate inline levels)

steps: Lock the mutex at this+0x38 via 0x60d5230 (0x6070c6a).
Loop (0x6070c88..0x6070cb5): for shard i in 0..(1 << shard_bits)-1, `xchg %rcx,(%rax)` with rcx = 0 — each shard's counter for the id becomes 0 and its old value is added into rbx (u64 wrap).
Unlock via 0x60d52f0 (0x6070cba) and return rbx, the sum over all shards.

Forward (0x6070cbf..0x6070d63): delegate = *(this+0x28); if null or ticker_id > 0xb1, return the sum. The delegate chain is reset via slot 0xb8 with value 0: the same devirtualization check as set-ticker (0x6070cd9..0x6070cee), inline lock + set_core(delegate, id, 0) + unlock (0x6070cf0..0x6070d0c), a second inline level (0x6070d11..0x6070d47), then a virtual CALL to the third delegate's slot 0xb8 with value 0 (0x6070d4c..0x6070d5d). These are calls, not tail jumps, because the sum in rbx must survive to the return.

Exception path: landing pads at 0x6070d7a (jmp 0x6070c2a) and 0x6070d86 (jmp 0x6070c3a); the shared fragment at 0x6070c2a..0x6070c4a has two identical entries (unlock the mutex at r13, _Unwind_Resume).

record_hist_0x606fef0.signature: (this: StatisticsImpl*, hist_id: u32, value: u64) -> void
steps: Gate (0x606fef4..0x606fef8): the enable byte at this+0x20 must be > 1 (cmp $0x1, jbe 0x606ff88); level 1 records ticks only, level 0 records nothing. There is no hist_id bound check before the record call.

Shard pick (0x606ff0c): call the CPU picker 0x60d5cd0; a negative return jumps to the fallback at 0x606ff90 (call 0x61c4080, Park-Miller step, store back, mask) — the same code as record_tick's fallback.

Record call (0x606ff17..0x606ff52): address = *(this+0x60) + shard*0xce40 + 0x598 + hist_id*0x3c8; load the record's vtable (first qword) and `call *0x20(%rax)` with (record, value) — the HistogramImpl record slot 0x606b130.

Forward (0x606ff55..0x606ff77): if hist_id <= 0x33 and *(this+0x28) is non-null, tail-jump to the delegate's slot 0xd8 with (delegate, hist_id, value). The 0x33 bound gates only the forward, not the local record.

record_hist_devirt_0x606ffd0.signature: (this: StatisticsImpl*, hist_id: u32, value: u64) -> void
steps: Devirtualization guard (0x606ffde..0x606fff5): load this's vtable slot 0xd8 and compare it against the local 0x606fef0; if it differs, restore the registers and `jmp *%rax` (0x6070078..0x607007f) — a virtual dispatch to the overriding slot 0xd8 with (this, hist_id, value).

Inline body (0x606fffb..0x607006d): otherwise the same body as slot 0xd8 — gate byte > 1, CPU pick (0x6070003) or LCG fallback (0x6070088), record call *0x20, forward to the delegate's slot 0xd8 when hist_id <= 0x33.
Lock the SOURCE's mutex (rsi+0x38) via 0x60d5230 (0x6070b58). The out Status is the first argument, the source the second.
Ticker loop (0x6070b60..0x6070b75): for id in 0..0xb1, set_core(source, id, 0) — every ticker on every shard becomes 0.
Histogram loop (0x6070b77..0x6070be5): for hist_id in 0..0x33, for each shard, call the record's vtable slot 0x10 (locked init/clear, 0x606b0c0) with (record) — `call *0x10(%rax)` at 0x6070bb4.
Write Status OK into out (0x6070be7..0x6070c05): code 0, subcode 0, state null; unlock the source mutex; return. No delegate walk, no enable-byte check.
Exception path: landing pad at 0x6070c1e (mov %rax,%rbx; jmp 0x6070b1c); the fragment at 0x6070b1c..0x6070b2e unlocks the source mutex (pointer saved at 0x18(%rsp)) and resumes unwinding.

reset_cleanup_0x6070b1c.contract: Reset's exception cleanup: unlock the source mutex (pointer saved at 0x18(%rsp)), then _Unwind_Resume with the exception in rbx. Reached by a tail jump from reset's landing pad at 0x6070c1e.

reset_cleanup2_0x6070c2a.contract: Shared unlock + resume fragment with two identical entries (0x6070c2a and 0x6070c3a): unlock the mutex at r13, then _Unwind_Resume with the exception in rbx. It serves slot 0xc0's two landing pads (0x6070d7a -> 0x6070c2a, 0x6070d86 -> 0x6070c3a); its FDE sits immediately after reset's, but reset itself uses reset_cleanup (0x6070b1c), not this fragment.

set_cleanup_0x6070d92.contract: Slot 0xb8's exception cleanup: two identical entries (0x6070d92 and 0x6070da2), each unlocking the mutex at r13 and then _Unwind_Resume with the exception in rbx. Reached from set-ticker's landing pads at 0x6070e82 (jmp 0x6070d92) and 0x6070e8e (jmp 0x6070da2).

stats_name_0x606fa20.contract: Returns the address of the string "BasicStatistics" at 0x432248 (lea 0x432248(%rip), %rax; ret). The same address holds the start of the ticker-name table ("rocksdb.l1.hit", "rocksdb.number.keys.updated", ... follow it).

delegate_getter_0x606fa30.contract: Returns *(this+0x28) — the delegate pointer, or null.

hist_id_check_0x606fa40.contract: Returns hist_id <= 0x33 (52 valid histogram ids, 0..51). This is the bound the record routines use to gate the delegate forward.

steps: Enable byte at this+0x20 := 3 (movb $0x3, 0x6071a32).
Options vector at this+0x8/+0x10 := {0, 0}; this+0x18 := 0 (0x6071a36..0x6071a60).

Delegate shared_ptr moved in from the 2nd argument: *(this+0x28) := arg+0x00 (the Statistics*), *(this+0x30) := arg+0x08 (the control block); the source's first 16 bytes are then zeroed with a 16-byte store (0x6071a4d..0x6071a76). CORRECTION to #3386, which called this field a string: it is a shared_ptr<Statistics> — the ctor moves a {ptr, control} pair, the record routines dereference *(this+0x28) as a vtable-bearing object, the dtor releases the control at +0x30, and slot 0x88 returns the pointer.
Mutex at this+0x38 initialized via 0x60d50c0 (0x6071a73..0x6071a7c).
Shard store at this+0x60 built via 0x60716d0 (0x6071a81..0x6071a85): shard count bits 3 when the hardware count is <= 8, else the smallest bits >= 4 with 2**bits >= hw (per #3386).

Appends the "StatisticsOptions" record via 0x6099ce0(this, name, &this+0x28, 0x6506200) (0x6071a8a..0x6071af1): the name string is built on the stack from .rodata 0x4539e0 (16 bytes) plus 's' at +0x10, i.e. the 17-byte name "StatisticsOptions"; the record stores the address of the delegate shared_ptr field.
The ctor's trailing cleanup fragment at 0x6071b60 (outside the ctor FDE) is not excerpted.
vptr := base-class vtable (lea 0x64d2d78 + 0x10, 0x6070eb5..0x6070ec4).

Shard store (0x6070ebc..0x6070f2c): for each shard, walk its 53 histogram records from the end and call each record's dtor through its vtable unless the vtable is the shared 0x5d89570 (the no-op check at 0x6070f00..0x6070f0e), then free the store via 0x60d5db0 (free).
Mutex at this+0x38 destroyed via 0x60d5170 (0x6070f31..0x6070f35).

Delegate shared_ptr released (0x6070f3a..0x6070f80): control block at this+0x30; when its counts are exactly 0x100000001 the fast path at 0x6071002 runs, otherwise the use count at +8 is decremented under the shared lock (0x6070f5e..0x6070f7a, with the 0x64ed290 guard). This is the release half of the ctor's move-in.
vptr := Configurable base 0x64d3420 + 0x10 and the options vector at this+0x8/+0x10 destroyed (0x6070f80..0x6070fc6 and following).

hist_record_0x606b130.contract: HistogramImpl slot 0x20 (called by record_hist's *0x20 dispatch and by the +8 thunk 0x606b1c0). Bucket index via 0x606afa0(boundaries vector 0x6505d20, value) (0x606b138..0x606b147); buckets[index]++ at record+0x28+index*8 (0x606b14c..0x606b158); min := value when value < min (0x606b15b..0x606b1a0), max := value when value > max (0x606b164..0x606b1ad); count++ (0x606b16d..0x606b175); sum += value (0x606b179..0x606b184); sum_sq += value*value (0x606b180..0x606b18f), all u64 wrap. The value is treated as a u64 throughout: integer compares, adds and multiply — no float conversion anywhere on this path.

hist_bucket_index_0x606afa0.contract: Lower_bound over the 109 boundaries at 0x6505d20. When value >= the ceiling (the qword at holder+0x18, 13000000000000000000), return count-1 = 108 (0x606afb8..0x606afc2); otherwise binary-search the first boundary >= value (0x606afc8..0x606b012). Exactly one direct caller: hist_record at 0x606b147.

hist_locked_init_0x606b0c0.contract: HistogramImpl slot 0x10: lock the record's mutex at +0x3a0 with pthread_mutex_lock directly (throwing system_error on failure, 0x606b0d7..0x606b0f7), call the shared init 0x606b020 on record+8 (0x606b0e0..0x606b0e4), unlock via pthread_mutex_unlock (tail jump 0x606b0f2). This is what reset calls per record through the vtable slot 0x10.

hist_shared_init_0x606b020.contract: Shared record init: min := *(0x6505d38) (the ceiling, 13000000000000000000); max := 0, count := 0, sum := 0, sum_sq := 0; buckets[0..bucket_count-1] := 0, where bucket_count is READ from inner+0x390 and is not written by this routine. Called by locked init (0x606b0e4) and tail-jumped to from bucket-count init 0x606b080 (0x606b09d).

boundary_gen_0x606bf10.contract: Histogram boundary generator, run once by the static init 0x606c140 (.init_array 0x63f3978). Seeds [1, 2] from .rodata 0x453950 into a fresh 0x10-byte allocation (0x606bf3e..0x606bf57); cur (a double, starting at 2.0) *= 1.5 (constant 0x4596c8) each step until cur >= 2**64 (constant 0x459090, 1.8446744073709552e19); each value is truncated toward zero to a u64 (the >= 2**63 path at 0x606c075 subtracts 2**63 (constant 0x459360) then xors the sign bit back in); values above 109 are truncated to 3 significant digits (the divide-by-10 loop at 0x606c006..0x606c039); on exit the last boundary is stored at holder+0x18 (the ceiling) and the first at holder+0x20 (0x606c0d8..0x606c0e7). Result: 109 boundaries, first 1, last 13000000000000000000.

boundaries.note: Re-derived by the model (tools/stats_write_side_115.py histogram_boundaries) from the generator algorithm above; count, first/last and the spot values match #3371's pinned boundaries.tsv values.

shard_layout.ticker_area: shard + id*8, ids 0..0xb1 valid, 179 slots physically (0x598 bytes)
shard_layout.histogram_area: shard + 0x598 + id*0x3c8, ids 0..0x33 valid, 53 records physically (0x598 + 53*0x3c8 == 0xce00)
shard_layout.tail: shard + 0xce00..0xce40 (0x40 bytes) is not examined; its contents are an open unknown (carried from #3392).
shard_layout.note: The ticker area physically holds 179 counters (0..178) while only 0..177 are valid; the histogram area physically holds 53 records (0..52) while only 0..51 are valid. set_core performs no bound check, so an id of 178 writes the 179th ticker slot and an id >= 179 would index into the histogram records.

enable_byte.levels: 0 = record nothing; 1 = tickers only (slot 0xb0 requires nonzero); >= 2 = tickers and histograms (slots 0xd8/0xd0 require > 1). The locked set/get-reset/reset slots (0xb8/0xc0/0xe0) do not consult the byte at all.
enable_byte.note: Which routine writes the byte besides the ctor is an open unknown; the remaining unmapped slots (0x10..0x90 except 0x70/0x88, 0xc8) are the candidates.

mutex_lock_0x60d5230.contract: pthread_mutex_lock wrapper (re-shipped from #3362/#3378); return codes 0 and 0x6e are accepted, any other prints 'pthread %s: %s' and aborts. It never throws a C++ exception, so the accessors' landing pads cover the builder/delegate calls, not the lock.

mutex_unlock_0x60d52f0.contract: pthread_mutex_unlock wrapper (re-shipped from #3362/#3378); same accept/abort discipline as the lock wrapper, never throws.

unknowns: The public C++ names of the six write routines are not established from the stripped binary; they are described by observed behaviour, signatures and vtable slots, not by source-level names.
Which routine writes the enable byte at +0x20 besides the ctor (a setter is the natural candidate; the unmapped slots 0x10..0x90 except 0x70/0x88 and 0xc8 are not mapped here).
The 0x40 tail at the end of each 0xce40-byte shard (0xce00..0xce40) is not examined; its contents are open (carried from #3392).
The bucket_count field at record+0x390 is read by the shared init and never written by it; its writer is an open unknown (likely the shard-store builder 0x60716d0 or the bucket-count init 0x606b080).

The exact _Hash_bytes output for a given pthread_self is not byte-verified against a live run (the seed is thread-dependent); the model implements the documented libstdc++ MurmurHash64A algorithm and only its determinism and range are tested.

The other three direct callers of the CPU picker (0x5f0aa40, 0x605e17b, 0x61c1e24) and the other 14 direct callers of the LCG seed accessor are other per-CPU / per-thread users; their routines are not mapped here.
Which landing pad covers which call site inside the locked routines is inferred from the register and mutex state, not read from the LSDA; the fragments' shapes and jump targets are pinned.
The histogram record path treats its third argument as a u64 throughout (integer compares, adds, multiply); no caller that passes a double's bit pattern was examined.
set_core performs no bound check: ids >= 179 index past the ticker area into the histogram records (observed addressing, not exercised).
The remaining StatisticsImpl vtable slots (0x10..0x90 except 0x70/0x88, 0xc8) are not mapped here.
The ctor's trailing cleanup fragment at 0x6071b60 (outside the ctor FDE) is not excerpted.

The +0x28 delegate is moved in from the creator's options struct; which construction paths install a non-null delegate (beyond the factory host, which passes its own options through) is not traced here.
